ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Sick Visit — Duke Kahanamoku

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for vomiting and diarrhea on heart failure medicines

text.paragraph: Vomiting and diarrhea for two days. [S]

Mr. Kahanamoku, a 66-year-old man with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, called the heart failure nurse and was seen the same day. Two days ago he began vomiting and then had watery diarrhea, five or six times a day, without blood. Several people at his workplace have had the same illness this week. He has kept down only small sips of water since yesterday and has not taken his morning medicines today, but he took all of them yesterday, including spironolactone, which was started nine days ago. His home weight is 2.2 kg below his dry weight. He feels lightheaded on standing. He has no chest pain, palpitations, breathlessness, ankle swelling or fainting, and no fever above 38 degrees. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-04-22; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Tired but alert; seated blood pressure 102/62, pulse 96, temperature 37.6
Lying 108/66 mmHg, pulse 88; standing at three minutes 90/58 mmHg, pulse 108, with lightheadedness
Dry mucous membranes; jugular venous pressure not seen at 45 degrees
Soft, mildly tender throughout, no guarding; active bowel sounds

Breathlessness on exertion for six weeks (paddling out, walking uphill, finishing his morning swim), with ankle swelling by evening and tiredness, five years after a heart attack; cause to be determined
S — Synthetic presenting problem, resolved at the second visit when the echocardiogram and cardiology established heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
Coronary artery disease with an old anterior myocardial infarction five years ago, treated with medicines; synthetic modern episode linked to the documented heart attack of 1952
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the 1952 heart attack remains D in the history.
Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction from ischemic cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 30% with a thinned, akinetic anterior wall and apex), NYHA class III at diagnosis
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the second visit; no claim that he had heart failure in his lifetime.
Iron deficiency without anemia (ferritin 62 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 16%)
S — Synthetic finding at the heart failure workup.

Viral gastroenteritis for two days, with volume depletion, potassium 5.5 mmol/L and a rise in creatinine on sacubitril-valsartan, spironolactone, empagliflozin and furosemide; settled with sick-day rules
S — Synthetic intercurrent problem at an unscheduled visit; it follows from his heart failure medicines and does not echo a documented illness.

list.item:
Viral gastroenteritis with volume depletion and a raised potassium (A08.4). A self-limited viral illness, as among his co-workers, with volume depletion: orthostatic fall in blood pressure, weight 2.2 kg below dry weight, sodium 133 mmol/L, creatinine 1.52 mg/dL from 1.16 and potassium 5.5 mmol/L, from reduced kidney blood flow on four medicines that act on the kidney. The ECG shows no changes of hyperkalemia. He can drink small amounts and does not need hospital care today. [S]
Sick-day rules: hold empagliflozin, furosemide, spironolactone and sacubitril-valsartan until he is eating and drinking normally for a day.
Halve carvedilol for two days while he is lightheaded, then return to the full dose.
Oral rehydration solution in small amounts often, about 2 liters today; bland food as tolerated.
Restart the held medicines one day after the illness settles, and weigh daily.
Recheck potassium and creatinine at the review in five days, or sooner if he cannot keep fluids down.

Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (I50.22). Dry, not congested. [S]
Call if his weight rises more than 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in a week after restarting.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure (2022); 2024 ACC Expert Consensus Decision Pathway for Treatment of Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction (2024)

Follow-up: Heart failure nurse telephone call tomorrow. Review in five days with a metabolic panel. Go to the emergency department for fainting, vomiting that prevents any fluid intake, palpitations, weakness or chest pain. Next scheduled visit 2026-04-27: two-week review, five days after the sick visit: kidney function and potassium, medicine doses, lipids, and cardiac rehabilitation adapted to the ocean. [S]
